plan.blog_title: Scaling RAG for Enterprise Knowledge Management
plan.audience: CTOs, Data Architects, and Senior AI Engineers

tasks.title: When Hallucinations Cost Millions
tasks.goal: Hook the reader by highlighting the financial and operational risks of ungrounded LLMs.
bullets: Contrast the speed of AI-driven decision-making with the catastrophic cost of a hallucinated compliance report.
Reference the 'Work AI Index 2026' findings regarding the 11-hour-per-week productivity gain from grounded AI.
Define the enterprise imperative: shifting from experimental RAG prototypes to production-grade knowledge architectures.

tasks.title: How Vector Representations Encode Business Meaning
tasks.goal: Explain the technical foundation of embeddings and vector search.
bullets: Detail how embedding models transform unstructured enterprise documentation into high-dimensional numerical vectors.
Analyze the role of semantic similarity in retrieval versus traditional keyword-based search.
Discuss the findings of Volodymyr Mudryi regarding the selection of embedding models based on intent vs. lexical matching.

tasks.title: Architecting the High-Performance Vector Database
tasks.goal: Discuss the infrastructure requirements for enterprise-scale retrieval.
bullets: Examine the transition from legacy key-value stores to specialized vector database solutions.
Highlight the latency requirements for real-time personalization, citing the Myntra case study where lookup latency dropped from 8.5ms to 0.8ms.
Evaluate the trade-offs between throughput capacity and query latency in high-concurrency environments.

tasks.title: Comparing Naive, Agentic, and Streaming RAG Patterns
tasks.goal: Provide a comparative analysis of modern RAG architectures.
bullets: Comparison Table: Naive RAG vs. Agentic RAG vs. Event-Driven RAG (evaluating cost, latency, complexity, and accuracy).
Explain the cost disparity between basic pipelines ($0.001/query) and complex agentic workflows.
Discuss the impact of architectural choice on total cost of ownership (TCO).

tasks.title: Synchronizing Operational Intelligence via Event Streams
tasks.goal: Explain the necessity of real-time data synchronization for RAG.
bullets: Analyze the limitations of static, batch-processed document indexing.
Describe the integration of event streaming platforms with vector databases to ensure context freshness.
Explain how real-time ingestion reduces the window for stale, hallucinated AI outputs in compliance and developer tooling.

tasks.title: Deploying Developer Copilots That Actually Work
tasks.goal: Demonstrate the real-world application of RAG in technical environments.
bullets: Examine the workflow of internal developer copilots that index live codebase documentation and Jira tickets.
Case Study: Analyze how digital-native firms implement automated compliance checkers that query updated regulatory databases.
Discuss the trade-offs in retrieval precision when dealing with highly domain-specific technical jargon.

tasks.title: The Path Toward Deterministic Enterprise AI
tasks.goal: Provide an actionable roadmap for readers to improve their RAG implementation.
bullets: Recommendation: Prioritize data freshness and embedding model evaluation over model parameter size.
Prediction: The shift toward agentic frameworks will necessitate a focus on observability and retrieval-traceability.
Actionable Step: Conduct a baseline latency audit of your current retrieval pipeline this week to identify bottleneck stages.

plan.keyword_strategy: Primary keyword 'RAG' is introduced in the title and opening. 'Vector database' and 'embeddings' are introduced in the grounding and architecture sections to maintain technical relevance without stuffing.
